### AI Policy

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Has journal-specific AI policy?** | *(see summary — defaults to publisher-level policy unless a journal-specific override was found)* |
| **Explicit permission gate?** | conditional |
| **Leniency (1-5)** | 3 |
| **Summary** | Publisher-level MDPI policy (no IJERPH-specific variant found). AI/LLM tools may assist manuscript preparation but cannot be listed as authors; use beyond basic language editing (grammar/formatting, no disclosure needed) must be disclosed with a description of how/where used, typically in Materials & Methods; authors remain fully responsible for content originality/validity. Reviewers are explicitly barred from using GenAI/LLMs to prepare review reports, citing confidentiality/data-protection risk. This is 'disclose and remain responsible' rather than an outright ban or fully open policy, hence leniency 3. Could not confirm an IJERPH-specific page distinct from the site-wide MDPI ethics policy - mdpi.com/ethics and the AI-authorship announcement both returned HTTP 403 on direct fetch, so this is reconstructed from WebSearch snippets of those pages plus a third-party LibGuide summary, not a direct primary read. |
| **Source URL** | https://www.mdpi.com/about/announcements/5687 (via cross-source summary; direct fetch 403'd) and https://libguides.iou.edu.gm/c.php?g=1482669&p=11059956 |

### Preprint Policy

> AI-research note (not broken down per-stage): Yes (publisher-level MDPI policy, not IJERPH-specific). Preprints are permitted provided the posted version has not itself been peer-reviewed; authors must disclose the preprint DOI/licensing at submission or during review, and must not update the preprint with revised versions while under confidential peer review. MDPI operates its own preprint server (Preprints.org) that authors can post to after submission.
> Source: https://www.mdpi.com/ethics (fetch blocked, 403; content reconstructed from WebSearch snippets of mdpi.com/ethics and preprints.org/instructions-for-authors)

**Current positioning (what the journal accepts now):** Journal remains active and publishing as of 2026 (Volume 23 in progress), despite being delisted from Clarivate Web of Science (SCIE/SSCI) in Feb 2023 for 'content relevance' concerns - publications judged outside declared scope. Still indexed in Scopus (per Chinese-source commentary, Scopus indexing was 'under reevaluation/on hold' as of a Jan 2024 report), PubMed/MEDLINE, and Embase. Monthly publication volume reportedly collapsed from near 2,000 papers/month pre-delisting to roughly 200/month afterward (per Zhihu analysis), i.e. MDPI sharply tightened intake post-delisting. A new Editor-in-Chief (Paul R. Ward) was appointed September 2025, explicitly framed by MDPI/commentators as a reform effort aimed at regaining SCI re-listing - this is a live, unresolved repositioning, not a settled status.

**Methods noted as welcome (qualitative — not a scored 0-5 table, see Methodological Preferences below):** Cross-sectional survey / questionnaire studies (very common per forum commentary), Occupational health & workplace mental health/stress studies (multiple active 2025-2026 special issues: 'Occupation, Mental Health and Well-Being', 'Work Psychology and Occupational Health 2nd Edition', 'Mental Health and Wellbeing in High-Risk Occupational Groups', 'Emerging Issues in Occupational Health Psychology'), Environmental epidemiology / exposure studies, Public-health intervention and policy evaluation

### Reviewer Pool Characteristics

小木虫/fabiaoji consensus: reviewers focus heavily on (1) claims lacking supporting evidence and (2) formatting/sentence-structure/organization issues; comments described as ranging from 'quite fair-minded' to inconsistent; strong emphasis that manuscripts must visibly connect to 'public health' relevance or risk being seen as scope-mismatched. No Reddit r/AskAcademia discussion of IJERPH specifically was found despite targeted search - treat the English-language cross-check as a null result, not an omission.

**Fields deliberately left blank, and why:**
- **peer_review.type (single vs double blind, confirmed IJERPH-specific)**: mdpi.com/journal/ijerph/about and mdpi.com/ethics both returned HTTP 403 on direct WebFetch; only WebSearch snippets of general MDPI-wide process were available, not an IJERPH-specific confirmation of blind type.
- **experiential.desk_reject_pct (aggregate rate)**: SciRev lists this journal's rejection rate as 'n/a'; only a single first-hand anecdote of a 3-day desk reject was found on fabiaoji.com, insufficient to construct a rate.
- **cross_language_checked: Reddit r/AskAcademia**: Targeted searches (site:reddit.com IJERPH MDPI; reddit AskAcademia IJERPH) returned zero relevant results - genuinely no English-language forum discussion found, not a search failure to report honestly.
- **ai_policy.source_url (IJERPH-specific AI policy page)**: No IJERPH-specific AI policy distinct from the site-wide MDPI ethics/announcement pages was located; both candidate primary pages (mdpi.com/ethics, mdpi.com/about/announcements/5687) returned HTTP 403 on direct fetch and had to be reconstructed from WebSearch snippets/third-party summaries only.

**Cross-language checks performed (mandatory per methodology):**
- 小木虫 muchong.com: multiple threads found on MDPI review timelines and IJERPH-specific submission advice (scope framing, reviewer focus) - useful qualitative signal
- fabiaoji.com: one detailed IJERPH review-log page found with concrete review-time and fee numbers, plus one desk-reject anecdote
- 知乎 zhihu.com: multiple articles/threads on the 2023 WoS delisting, causes, and the Sept 2025 new editor-in-chief reform effort - useful for positioning/reputation, direct zhihu.com/question fetch was blocked (403) so relied on WebSearch snippets and zhuanlan.zhihu.com analysis articles
- Reddit r/AskAcademia: 0 results for IJERPH-specific discussion despite multiple query variants - genuine null result
